title: California Makes Diwali an Official Statewide Holiday, Joining Pennsylvania and Connecticut
excerpt: The law signed by Governor Newsom allows state employees to take paid leave and public schools to close on the Festival of Lights, starting in 2026.
body:
• California became the third US state to designate Diwali as an official state holiday after Governor Gavin Newsom signed Assembly Bill 268 into law.
  • Starting in 2026, state employees can take paid time off and public schools and community colleges may close on Diwali.
  • California is home to nearly 960,000 Indian Americans — about 20 percent of the national total — making it the state with the largest Indian-origin population in the country.
  • Pennsylvania was the first state to recognize Diwali in 2024, followed by Connecticut in 2025.

California has officially designated Diwali as a statewide holiday, making it the third state in the nation to recognize the Festival of Lights. Governor Gavin Newsom signed Assembly Bill 268 into law in October 2025, with the measure taking effect on January 1, 2026.

Under the new law, public schools and community colleges are authorized to close on Diwali, and state employees may take a paid day off. Students who observe the holiday will be excused from attendance without penalty. Courts, however, remain open as Diwali is excluded from the judicial holiday calendar.

A Milestone for South Asian Communities

The bill was co-authored by Assemblymember Ash Kalra, a Democrat representing San Jose, and Assemblymember Darshana Patel of San Diego. Both lawmakers framed the legislation as a landmark moment for cultural inclusion in the state.

"According to a 2025 Pew Research Center survey, about 960,000 residents of Indian origin live in California — roughly 20 percent of the nation's total of 4.9 million Indian Americans."

"According to a 2025 Pew Research Center survey, about 960,000 residents of Indian origin live in California — roughly 20 percent of the nation's total of 4.9 million Indian Americans."

"To have South Asian children be able to celebrate and share it with others proudly is a significant moment."

— Ash Kalra, California Assemblymember

Kalra said the holiday "will uplift its message to the hundreds of thousands of Californians that celebrate and help introduce it to many throughout our diverse state." He added that California should "embrace Diwali and its diversity, not keep it hidden in darkness."

Hindu American organizations, including the Hindu American Foundation and the Coalition of Hindus in North America, advocated for the legislation. Samir Kalra, managing director of the Hindu American Foundation, said the provisions allowing students to take the day off without consequence and state employees to take paid leave "are important leaps toward making Diwali truly accessible to those who celebrate."

Why It Matters for the Diaspora

California has the largest Indian American population of any state. According to a 2025 Pew Research Center survey, about 960,000 residents of Indian origin live in California — roughly 20 percent of the nation's total of 4.9 million Indian Americans. Nearly half of those who identify as Indian alone practice Hinduism.

Diwali derives from the Sanskrit word "Deepavali," meaning "a row of lights." The festival symbolizes the triumph of light over darkness and knowledge over ignorance. It is celebrated by Hindus, Sikhs, Jains, and Buddhists, typically falling in October or November based on the Hindu lunar calendar.

Gopala Ajjarapu, president of Sri Satyanarayana Swamy Devasthanam, a Hindu temple in Milpitas, said the new law made him "proud and happy." He called it a sign that the United States, a "country of immigrants," is becoming "even more inclusive."

A Growing National Movement

Pennsylvania became the first state to declare Diwali an official holiday in 2024. Connecticut followed in 2025 with Public Act 25-59. North Carolina has also celebrated Diwali as a state observance. At the local level, New York City schools close on Diwali, and districts in New Jersey and Texas have adopted similar policies.

Despite the growing state-level recognition, Diwali remains absent from the federal holiday calendar. Federal offices, courts, and financial markets remain open on the day. Advocates have pushed for national recognition, but no federal legislation has advanced.

What's Next

The first official observance of Diwali as a California state holiday will fall in 2026. The holiday's date shifts annually — it is determined by the position of the moon and typically lands between mid-October and mid-November. For South Asian families across the state, the formal recognition marks a shift from informal celebration to institutional acknowledgment of one of the world's most widely observed festivals, with an estimated one billion people celebrating each year.
